## Part 1 — Key facts

All ten key facts are present and correctly stated on the right basis and period. Notable checks: the constant-currency and free-cash-flow figures are both labelled non-GAAP; the $2.40bn legal charge and $1.18bn severance are tied to Q2 2026 and the May 2026 reduction; the capex outlook is correctly described as *narrowed* (lower end raised from $125bn to $130bn).

## Part 2 — Claims

37 of 38 atomic claims check out against the release. The one exception is in the opening headline, where the cost increase is presented as the driver of the free-cash-flow decline. The release shows operating cash flow *rose* (to $31.86bn from $25.56bn), and free cash flow fell because of $30.12bn of property and equipment purchases plus $0.96bn of finance-lease principal — not because of the 55% cost growth (much of which is non-cash, e.g. $7.66bn share-based compensation and $6.36bn depreciation). The release asserts no such causal link. The operating-income half of that sentence is fine.

Everything else — segment revenue and income, RL loss, R&D/G&A lines, engagement metrics, all four outlook items, the balance-sheet and financing figures, the $8,549m prior-year free cash flow comparison and the $24.9bn rounding of $24,910m net debt proceeds — is directly stated in the release.

facts.evidence: Revenue was $60.80 billion, up 28% year over year.
Net income was $15,848 million, down 14%, and diluted EPS was $6.18 versus $7.14.

Family of Apps revenue was $60,370 million, of which advertising was $59,363 million (up 27%; up 26% excluding foreign exchange effect, non-GAAP) and other revenue $1,007 million. FoA income from operations was $23,394 million versus $24,971 million.
Income from operations was $18,775 million, down 8%; operating margin was 31%, versus 43% in the prior-year quarter.
Q3 2026 revenue guidance is $61–64 billion, assuming foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year growth.
Total costs and expenses were $42.03 billion, up 55%, including $2.40 billion of charges related to legal proceedings and $1.18 billion of severance tied to the May 2026 headcount reduction.

Cash flow from operating activities was $31.86 billion; free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $784 million.
full year 2026 capex, including finance lease principal payments, is $130–145 billion, narrowed from $125–145 billion
Family daily active people averaged 3.60 billion in June 2026, up 3%.
